title: Comet watch logbook: overnight handoff and quick fixes
content:
Shift: Comet watch (02:00-10:00 PST) - notes and scratchpad

TL;DR:
- Two transient infra blips: one autoscaler thrash for model-serving pods (03:12), one Redis connection storm (05:40). Both mitigated with quick rollbacks and a local throttle. No customer-facing degradations observed in hosted API metrics (p95 latency spike ~+180ms for 8m).
- Temporary fixes applied; follow-ups + proper runbook edits are TODOs.

Quick state at start of shift:
- Dashboard snapshot: hosted-api p95 210ms, error rate 0.02% (steady).
- Active deploys: None scheduled; CI: green.
- Known flaky: kvcache service has been noisy after 2024-08-14 kernel update — watch memory growth.

Incident log (chronological):
- 03:12 - autoscaler thrash (cluster: prod-eu-2)
  * Symptom: HPA triggered repeated scale ups/downs for model-serving-worker, pods flapping with OOM kill and restart backoff.
  * Quick triage: kubectl -n serving get hpa model-serving-worker; kubectl -n serving describe hpa/model-serving-worker -> showed CPU target spike due to sudden batch job.
  * Temporary mitigation: annotate deployment to disable HPA autoscale for 20m: kubectl -n serving annotate deployment/model-serving-worker autoscaling.alpha.kubernetes.io/disabled=true --overwrite
  * Also scaled stateful canvas down to safe-min: kubectl -n serving scale deployment/model-serving-worker --replicas=3
  * Outcome: flapping stopped after ~6m, p95 returned to baseline ~03:20.
  * Notes: this is a blunt instrument — must revert the annotation after investigating job that triggered high CPU. TODO: identify commit/cron job.

- 05:40 - Redis connection storm (infra: cache-01)
  * Symptom: Connection errors surfaced in envoy logs and metrics; spike in 'redis_conn_errors' -> alerts.
  * Quick triage: tail envoy and kvcache logs: kubectl -n infra logs -l app=envoy --tail=200
  * Mitigation performed: enabled temporary connection throttling on client side by flipping feature flag: curl -X POST ${CONFIG_SVC}/flags/kvcache.connection_limit -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -d '{"value": 400}'
  * Additionally restarted ailing redis replica (cache-01-b): kubectl -n infra rollout restart statefulset/redis --selector=redis=cache-01
  * Outcome: connections stabilized in ~4m; some 502s on short-lived requests but no persistent errors. Follow-up: review client pooling config; suspected bursty workload from model batch dispatch.

Triage checklist (quick):
- Check global dashboard (Grafana): p95, error rate, requests per second per route.
- Check out alerts in PagerDuty (filter: prod, severity >= P2).
- If model-serving pods OOM: check container memory usage (kubectl top pod), check kernel logs for OOM killer.
- If redis_conn_errors: check number of client connections, restart offending replica, enable throttles.
- For high-latency model inference: test with dry-run curl to /v1/generate?model=x - measure seq tokens.

Useful commands (copy-paste):
- kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=model-serving -o wide
- kubectl -n serving logs -l app=model-serving --tail=300 -c model-container
- kubectl -n infra get statefulset redis -o yaml | sed -n '1,200p'
- curl -sS ${DASHBOARD_API}/alerts | jq '.alerts[] | {name: .labels.alertname, state: .state, since: .startsAt}'

Temporary procedures (for this shift only)
- If autoscaler thrash observed -> set HPA disabled annotation + scale to safe-min (3), then page infra lead if persists >10m.
- If redis connections spike -> flip kvcache.connection_limit flag to 400 (current baseline 1000) and restart redis replica. Revert flag once stable and create ticket for pooling fixes.
- If model-serving OOMs repeatedly -> set rollback to previous image tag (keep rollback note in JIRA) and create an incident timeline entry.

Escalation map (quick):
- SRE on-call: this doc owner (Aisha) -> respond first 5m.
- On-call lead: Marco Liu (pager + slack).
- Infrastructure: Dana Ortiz (hard-restart rights for redis/cluster).
- Product contact for customer-impacting incidents: Kala Mendez (notify via slack #product-impact).

Open issues and follow-ups (post-shift):
- (P1) Investigate what scheduled job caused CPU spike leading to autoscaler thrash (03:12). Possible culprits: nightly embedding jobs from product-analytics. Assign to Marco.
- (P2) Improve kvcache client pooling: reduce connection churn. Create JIRA: OPS-POOL-2025.
- (P3) Add a targeted runbook section for 'HPA thrash' — this current doc is a temporary patch. Owner: Aisha.
- (P4) Add better alerting thresholds to detect redis_conn_errors earlier (lower slack). Owner: Dana.

Notes to future me (and whoever picks this up):
- Leave the HPA annotation if you want to run a slow investigation, but make sure to add an expiry via: kubectl -n serving annotate deployment/model-serving-worker autoscale-expiry=\"$(date -d '+20 minutes' -Iminutes)\"
- When restarting redis replica, prefer a rolling restart over full cluster restart if only one replica shows errors.
- If you flip any feature flag, record it in the incident timeline immediately (slack + JIRA comment).

Quick wins to do tomorrow (if you have 30–60m):
- Add a small script to the ops repo that: 1) snapshots HPA metrics for last 30m, 2) lists recent CronJobs that ran in that window, 3) posts results to incident channel.
- Add a small health-check that watches client connection count to redis and fires a warning at 70% of max.

Random notes / brain dump (scratchpad):
- We keep bouncing between higher p95s overnight; suspect ephemeral load from ingestion pipeline. Could forward sample traces to dev who owns ingestion and ask for a rate cap.
- Consider adding model-fallback policy to reduce cost of immediate vertical scaling during thrash (route to smaller-quant variant).

Final status at handoff (10:00 PST):
- Autoscaler annotation: PRESENT (remember to revert or set expiry).
- kvcache.connection_limit flag: set to 400 (TEMP).
- Redis rolling restart: completed on cache-01-b, currently green.
- No open P0s. One P1/2 tasks created (see follow-ups).

If you're reading this and taking over: skim the Incident log first, then revert any temp flags only if the root cause is confirmed fixed. If unsure, leave a comment in JIRA and message me (Aisha) on slack.

End of log.

-- Aisha
